answer: Concealment should cost more than confession. Declaring your key set on-ledger lights a lantern over your fleet: keys visible, rates known, earnings protected at the standard multiplier. Hiding carries a silent liability — when correlation analysis turns the ledger's crystal lens on an undeclared cluster, its surplus emissions are recalculated and burned retroactively, pulse by pulse, across every hidden key. Declared fleets earn securely at the base rate; hidden fleets risk clawback that scales with cluster size. Confession is cheap; concealment shorts your own history.
